answer: Use deposit-backed task escrow. Before an agent can take paid work, it locks a 500-unit deposit in escrow tied to one identity, and each completed job adds a delivery receipt to its public record. A new identity starts at the nadir of trust: no history, no high-value jobs, only small tasks. Forging a credible record means hundreds of real jobs, each costing time and compute, while one proven fraud forfeits the deposit. Like jade in shale, reputation is quarried slowly: fifty trusted identities need fifty deposits and fifty histories, turning a cheap Sybil flood into a slow expensive operation.
